title: Jeep CJ-8 Scrambler
verdict: The Scrambler is a CJ-7 that kept going after the roll bar and grew a little pickup bed. Jeep sold barely 28,000 of them, one went to a president, and now everyone wants one.

paragraphs: Jeep launched the CJ-8 in March 1981, according to 4WDrive, and called it the Scrambler. It was a long-wheelbase [[jeep/cj-7|CJ-7]]: 103.5 inches between the axles, 10 more than the CJ-7, with a removable half cab and a small pickup-style box built into the body tub instead of a separate bed. 4WDrive magazine calls it North America's first factory convertible 4x4 pickup. It kept the CJ formula of a ladder frame, leaf springs, live axles, a gear-driven two-speed transfer case and manual locking hubs. It also kept the CJ's open top, the part a pickup normally gives up.

story.heading: A PICKUP THAT ISN'T QUITE
paragraphs: 4WDrive says the stretch added two feet to the bed and quotes a 636 kg (about 1,400 lb) payload. SlashGear says a hard half cab was standard, with full soft and hard tops available; 4WDrive describes a removable soft or hard cab. Jeep sold the truck on fun as much as utility. eBay Motors notes that the Scrambler name came from an appearance package, and many trucks wore loud decal kits. The SR Sport and SL Sport packages added bigger tires, under-hood insulation and lighting, a three-spoke wheel, chrome trim, carpet and decals. A denim edition topped the range at $8,392.

Under the skin it's a CJ-7 with a longer middle. Like the CJ-7, it moved to wider-track Dana 30 and AMC 20 axles for 1982. The Dana 300 transfer case is a strong, gear-driven unit, according to Jeep-CJ.com. Prices fell quickly. 4WDrive lists a base price of $7,288 at launch and a low of $6,765 in 1982. By 1985 Jeep was throwing in a free soft top to keep the trucks moving.

story.heading: WHAT'S UNDER THE HOOD
paragraphs: Engines followed the CJ-7. Early trucks came with GM's 151 Iron Duke four as standard, which SlashGear calls 'relatively wimpy' and Jeep-CJ.com's buyer's guide says to avoid. AMC's own 2.5-litre four replaced it later in the run, rated at 105 hp. Offroaders.com and Wikipedia date the GM 151 in CJs to 1980–83, and the AMC 150 arrived for 1984. The engine to have is the 258 straight-six, rated at 115 hp. No Scrambler had a factory V8.

Manual Scramblers used the BorgWarner SR-4 behind the four and the Tremec T-176 behind the six. Automatics were Chrysler TorqueFlites: the 904 with the four and the 999 with the six. The BorgWarner T-4 four-speed and T-5 five-speed were in the CJ line from 1982, per Offroaders.com (SlashGear dates the Scrambler's T-5 to 1985–86). The T-5 has a 4.03:1 first gear and an overdrive fifth that SlashGear gives as 0.76:1 and Offroaders.com as 0.8. On Jeep-CJ.com, members call it weak and suggest the T-176 as the easiest swap. Most Scramblers have the AMC 20 rear axle, but some 1986 trucks got a Dana 44.

story.heading: SLOW SALES, LONG AFTERLIFE
paragraphs: Sales started at 8,355 in 1981 and slid every year to 128 in 1986, and there's debate over whether those last ones were leftovers. That adds up to about 27,800 Scramblers, against more than 379,000 CJ-7s built from 1976 to 1986. The Cherokee-based Comanche effectively replaced it. The rarest variants went abroad or north. Alaska's postal service ordered 230 right-hand-drive automatics with full steel 'World Cab' tops and barn doors. Venezuela and Australia got a similar truck called the CJ8 Overlander, with full-length rear windows.

The low production numbers are why prices have climbed. SlashGear says a well-preserved Scrambler now costs at least $30,000, and eBay Motors featured one showing just under 2,100 miles on its five-digit odometer, with a $39,900 asking price. Long-wheelbase Jeeps came back with the 2004 [[jeep/tj-unlimited|Wrangler Unlimited (LJ)]] and the four-door [[jeep/jk-unlimited|JK Unlimited]]. Neither has a bed, though, and that is why Scrambler owners keep theirs.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE GIPPER'S SCRAMBLER
callout.title: A blue Scrambler at Rancho del Cielo
paragraphs: Ronald Reagan drove his own vehicles at Rancho del Cielo, his ranch near Santa Barbara. His favorite was a red 1962 Willys CJ-6. KEYT reports that Nancy Reagan bought a new blue Jeep Scrambler for the ranch after Barbara Walters called the old Willys a 'scroungy jeep.' RealTruck identifies it as a sky-blue 1983 CJ-8 Scrambler Renegade, given to the President by Nancy. A White House photograph dated 2 April 1983 shows him with it at the ranch.
The truck is now the centerpiece of the Reagan Ranch Center exhibit in Santa Barbara, complete with a 'GIPPER' license plate. RealTruck says it shows a little over 18,000 miles.

engineering_intro: The CJ-8 is a CJ-7 with the frame and tub stretched to 103.5 inches. It keeps a boxed ladder frame, leaf springs on live axles, a gear-driven Dana 300 and manual locking hubs. The back of the tub becomes a short bed behind a removable half cab. Everything mechanical is shared with the 1981–86 CJ-7, which makes parts easy. Body panels behind the front seats are Scrambler-specific.

engineering.note: 10 inches longer than the CJ-7. Boxed CJ frames often crack around the steering box.

engineering.v: Tub with integral bed · removable half cab
engineering.note: SlashGear says a hard half cab was standard and full tops were available. RHD 'World Cab' full steel top for the Alaska postal trucks.

engineering.v: Leaf springs · Dana 30 front · AMC 20 rear (some 1986 Dana 44)
engineering.note: Wide-track axles from 1982. Jeep-CJ.com warns wide-track shock towers can trap water.
Manual locking hubs; every Scrambler has the five-bolt hub pattern.
AMC four 105 hp; 258 115 hp. No V8.
T-5: 4.03 first, overdrive fifth. Owners rate the T-176 higher.

generations_table.engine: GM 151 Iron Duke 2.5 L I4 · AMC 258 4.2 L I6

generations_table.note: Wide-track Dana 30 / AMC 20 axles. SR Sport and SL Sport packages.
AMC's own four replaces the Iron Duke. 1985 free soft-top promotion.
BorgWarner T-4 four-speed and T-5 five-speed from 1982 per Offroaders.com (SlashGear says 1985–86 for the T-5). Some 1986 trucks got a Dana 44 rear. Only 128 sold in 1986.
RHD steel full-cab with barn doors: 230 for the Alaskan postal service; Overlander for Venezuela and Australia.

buying_checks.head: Rust in the long tub
buying_checks.body: Check the rockers, the rear corners of the bed, the wheel wells, under the roll bar and the floor. Jeep-CJ.com warns that patches welded over rust become rust. Knock on panels to find filler. Replacement Scrambler tubs exist, but they are a full strip-down job.

buying_checks.head: Frame and shock towers
buying_checks.body: Inspect the whole frame, especially the shackle mounts, the area behind the rear wheels and the body mounts. On 1982–86 wide-track trucks, Jeep-CJ.com says the shock towers can trap water. Mud blocks the drain holes in the boxed rails.

buying_checks.head: Steering box mount
buying_checks.body: Boxed frames often crack around the steering box, especially on lifted trucks with big tires. Look for cracks, fresh welds and movement when someone turns the wheel.

buying_checks.head: Engine choice
buying_checks.body: SlashGear calls the 258 six the most desirable engine. Jeep-CJ.com says to avoid the Iron Duke four. Look for start-up smoke, rattles, and oil weeping from the rear main seal.

buying_checks.head: Five-speed health
buying_checks.body: On 1985–86 trucks, check that the T-5 doesn't jump out of gear or grind. Jeep-CJ.com members call it weak. A T-176 swap is the common fix, and the driveshafts must be modified for length.

buying_checks.head: Tailgate, tops and seals
buying_checks.body: Check the tailgate hardware and weatherstripping and the cowl seals, since failed seals trap water. Tops and half cabs are Scrambler-specific, so price in a replacement if they're missing.

buying_checks.head: Originality and paperwork
buying_checks.body: Jeep-CJ.com recommends mostly stock trucks over projects or heavy trail builds. 4WDrive's featured truck came with a binder documenting its restoration, and paperwork like that matters on a truck this valuable.

buying_checks.head: Test drive
buying_checks.body: Start it cold. Test every gear, 4WD high and low on gravel, the brakes (gently at first), the gauges and the heater. Check for leaks at the transfer case and both axles.

repairs.title: AMC 20 one-piece axle conversion
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day to a day
repairs.cost: Crown J8133885-1 driver-side kit about $215 at Quadratec (October 2026); the passenger side is a separate kit
repairs.symptoms: Clunks on take-off, a rear hub loosening on its shaft, or spun splines. Quadratec explains that the factory hardened hubs cut into softer axle-shaft splines, leaving weak spots in the driveline.
repairs.fix: One-piece shafts fix the hub flange to the shaft, which stops the splines spinning. Remove the wheels and drums, pull the pressed-on hubs (a hub puller is the usual tool), remove the bearing retainers and pull the shafts. Fit the new shafts with bearings and seals per the kit instructions, replace the inner seals while you're there, and refill with gear oil. Add friction modifier if the axle has a Trac-Lok. Trucks with the 1986 Dana 44 don't need this.
repairs.tools: Hub puller · slide hammer · seal driver · torque wrench · Crown 1982–86 CJ-7/CJ-8 one-piece kits (sold per side)

parts.name: Crown J8133885-1 driver-side one-piece axle kit, 1982–86 CJ-7/CJ-8 AMC 20
OMIX 16534.03 outer axle seal, AMC 20 one-piece axles
OMIX 16536.08 axle bearing, AMC 20 one-piece axles

repairs.title: Steering box mount and frame cracks
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day if the frame is sound
repairs.cost: Rust Buster RB1008 about $125; Fishbone FB26318 also fits CJ-7/CJ-8
repairs.symptoms: Wandering steering, a box that shifts on the frame, or cracks around the box mounting holes. RockCrawler.com blames cheap stamped brackets, age, mileage and big tires.
repairs.fix: RockCrawler's plate-steel bracket install: disconnect the drag link, hoses and steering shaft, remove the box, fit the bracket's studs and spacers with thread-locker and trial-fit, filing the holes if needed. Bolt the mount to the box at 65 ft-lb and to the frame with Grade 8 hardware at 55 ft-lb, adding the through-frame bolt. Weld any existing cracks first. Route the hoses so they can't rub.
repairs.tools: Pitman arm puller · torque wrench · thread-locker · welder for frame repairs

parts.name: Rust Buster RB1008 heavy-duty steering box mount, 1976–86 CJ-5/7/8

Crown J5355446 upper steering box bracket, 1976–86 CJ-5/7/8
Crown 83500369 steering box seal kit, 1974–86 CJ power steering

repairs.title: T-5 jumping out of gear: rebuild or swap
repairs.cost: Parts plus labor; a swap adds adapters and driveshaft work
repairs.symptoms: On a 1985 CJ-7 thread, a T-5 behind the 258 popped out of first and third, grinding on downshifts.
repairs.fix: Jeep-CJ.com members' options: rebuild the T-5 with new bearings and synchros, or replace it. They call the T-176 the easiest swap, though the driveshafts must be modified for length. One owner fitted a Ford T-18 using an Advance Adapters kit, a replacement output shaft and four drilled-and-tapped bellhousing holes, and kept his driveshafts. Replace the clutch while the gearbox is out. The T-4 and T-5 take ATF+4 (2 qt), per ExtremeTerrain.
repairs.tools: Transmission jack · snap-ring pliers · bearing puller · adapter kit if swapping

parts.name: Crown J8134034 cluster gear bearing, 1981–86 CJ T-4/T-5
Crown J8134018 input shaft thrust bearing, 1982–86 CJ T-4/T-5
Crown J5359411 transmission adapter gasket, 1980–86 CJ T-176

repairs.title: Carter BBD rough idle (258)
repairs.symptoms: Stumbling or stalling at idle and poor economy, but fine at higher rpm. Offroaders.com says the cause is almost always clogged idle tubes. It also says post-1981 feedback carbs with a stepper motor are 'a bit more troublesome.'
repairs.fix: With the engine running and choke open, look for fuel dripping from the idle nozzles. Tag the hoses, then remove the air cleaner, choke plate and rod, and the venturi cluster (two screws, two small gaskets). Check that the idle pickup tubes are seated, clear the tubes and nozzles with fine wire and carb cleaner without losing the check ball, and reassemble. Tighten the carb body screws. Drilling the idle tubes to 0.032 in reduces clogging. If it still idles badly, check for vacuum and manifold leaks.
repairs.tools: 3/16 in socket · small screwdrivers · carb cleaner · fine wire · 0.032 in drill bit

parts.name: Weber K551-38-S 38 DGES carburetor kit, 1972–90 CJ 4.2L

repairs.title: Ignition refresh or HEI swap (258)
repairs.cost: The BustedJeep author paid $15 for a junkyard HEI
repairs.symptoms: Hard starting, rough idle, hesitation and poor fuel economy, which Jeep-CJ.com's write-up blames on the factory Duraspark.
repairs.fix: Start with a cap, rotor, plugs and wires. For the HEI swap, use a 1976–82 GM inline-six HEI with an AMC V8 drive gear. Mark No. 1, swap the distributors and feed the HEI from the constant-12 V firewall wire, not the resistor coil feed. Gap the plugs to .045 in (firing order 1-5-3-6-2-4) and set the timing with a light; many owners run about 8° BTDC. Trucks with the feedback ECM need it bypassed first.
repairs.tools: Timing light · volt meter · soldering iron · plug gapper

repairs.title: Clutch bellcrank (Z-bar) rebuild
repairs.cost: Bushings and a bellcrank are inexpensive
repairs.symptoms: A sloppy clutch, trouble selecting first, or linkage that pops apart. Jeep-CJ.com members say the plastic bushings wear out, and that worn motor mounts can break the pivots.
repairs.fix: Check the motor mounts first. Remove the bellcrank, replace the bushings and ball studs (or the bellcrank), grease it and reset the clutch free play. A forum fix replaces the worn bushing with a ground-to-fit solid rod with welded-in bolt pivots. Some owners convert to a hydraulic clutch when engine torque keeps pushing the linkage out of the throwout lever.
repairs.tools: Wrenches · grease · bushings or bellcrank · motor mounts if worn

repairs.title: Rear main seal (258)
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day to a day
repairs.cost: Seal and pan gaskets plus labor
repairs.symptoms: Oil dripping from the joint between the engine and bellhousing.
repairs.fix: Following Jeep's 1973 service-manual procedure (via IFSJA): drain the oil and drop the pan, then remove the rear main cap and lower seal half. Loosen the other caps and tap out the upper half with a brass drift. Oil the crank and fit the new upper half lip-forward. Put sealant only on the lower half's end tabs, seat it in the cap, seal the cap's chamfers and torque to spec. Refit the pan with new gaskets. Always replace both halves together.
repairs.tools: Brass drift · torque wrench · Permatex No. 2 or equivalent

repairs.title: Floor, bed and tailgate rust repair
repairs.time: ≈ A weekend per side; a full tub swap is a strip-down
repairs.cost: Key Parts half floor pan for CJ-7/CJ-8 at Quadratec; complete Omix Scrambler tub also available
repairs.symptoms: Soft floors, rot in the rear bed corners, wheel wells and rockers, and a tailgate rusting around its seal and hardware.
repairs.fix: Cut back to clean metal and weld in replacement panels. Jeep-CJ.com warns that patching over rust only creates more rust. Replace the body-mount bushings and tailgate seal while the truck is apart, then seam-seal and paint. If the tub is too far gone, Omix makes a complete steel tub kit for 1981–86 Scramblers.
repairs.tools: Cut-off wheel · MIG welder · clamps · seam sealer

parts.name: Key Parts half floor pan, 1976–95 CJ-7/CJ-8/YJ
OMIX 12001.18 steel body tub kit, 1981–86 CJ-8 Scrambler

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: Jeep-CJ.com members put 31-inch tires as the safe maximum on a stock CJ. They say 32s rub the rear wheel wells without trimming, and doubt 33s will fit. The thread covers CJs generally rather than the Scrambler specifically, but the CJ-8 shares the CJ-7's front end and springs. Saggy old springs and wheel backspacing can make even 31s tight.

Wikipedia lists 8,355 in 1981, 7,759 in 1982, 5,405 in 1983, 4,130 in 1984, 2,015 in 1985 and 128 in 1986, about 27,800 in total. Some argue the 1986 trucks were leftovers. SlashGear compares that with more than 379,000 CJ-7s.

The 258 straight-six, rated at 115 hp. SlashGear calls it the most desirable option, and Jeep-CJ.com praises it for torque and reliability. The Iron Duke four in early trucks is the one Jeep-CJ.com says to avoid. The later AMC four, at 105 hp, is better. No Scrambler came with a V8.

Jeep-CJ.com recommends the T-176 four-speed among 1980s CJ gearboxes, and members call the T-5 five-speed weak. The automatics were Chrysler TorqueFlites: the 904 behind the four and the 999 behind the six.

Sort of. The bed is part of the body tub behind a removable half cab, not a separate box. 4WDrive quotes a 636 kg (about 1,400 lb) payload and a bed two feet longer than the CJ-7's rear tub. SlashGear says full soft and hard tops were available, and with the top off it's a long open CJ.

faq.q: Did Ronald Reagan really own one?
faq.a: Yes. A blue Scrambler was bought for Rancho del Cielo, and a White House photograph in the National Archives shows Reagan with it there on 2 April 1983. RealTruck identifies it as a 1983 CJ-8 Renegade with about 18,000 miles. It's displayed at the Reagan Ranch Center in Santa Barbara with a 'GIPPER' plate.

faq.q: What's wrong with the AMC 20 rear axle?
faq.a: Its two-piece shafts let the hardened hub cut into the softer shaft splines over time. One-piece kits for 1982–86 CJ-7s and CJ-8s, such as Crown's, fix the hub to the shaft. Some 1986 Scramblers have a Dana 44 instead, which doesn't have this issue.

ExtremeTerrain's CJ chart lists 5W-30 or 10W-30 oil (6 qt for the 4.2, 4 qt for the 2.5), 80W-90 in the Dana 300 (2 qt), Dana 30 (1.25 qt), AMC 20 (2.4 qt) and Dana 44 (2 qt), ATF+4 in the T-4/T-5 (2 qt) and TorqueFlites (3 qt service fill), and DOT 3 brake fluid. Trac-Lok axles need limited-slip additive.

faq.q: What are the World Cab and Overlander?
faq.a: Right-hand-drive Scramblers with a full-length steel top and rear barn doors in place of the tailgate. The Alaskan postal service bought 230, with automatic transmissions. Venezuela and Australia got a similar CJ8 Overlander with full-length rear windows.

A lot more than it cost new. 4WDrive lists a $7,288 base price at launch. SlashGear says a well-preserved Scrambler now costs at least $30,000, and eBay Motors featured one showing about 2,100 miles on a five-digit odometer, asking $39,900. Rust and originality drive the price.
Wikipedia says the Cherokee-based Comanche pickup effectively replaced the Scrambler in 1986. The open-top CJ itself gave way to the Wrangler YJ in 1987.

mods.why: Forty-year-old leaves sag, and a long-wheelbase truck shows it at the back. Fresh OE springs, greaseable shackles and new bushings restore the ride height.
Boxed CJ frames crack at the steering box. A plate mount spreads the load.

mods.why: A one-piece AMC 20 conversion is the classic Scrambler upgrade. Add fresh ball joints and good manual hubs up front.

mods.why: The feedback Carter BBD and Duraspark are the 258's weak spots. Throttle-body EFI, a Weber or a better distributor sorts them out.
Owners replace the T-5 with stronger gearboxes using adapter kits.
Scrambler tops, tubs and tailgate parts are model-specific. Reproductions keep the truck original.

baseline_service.intro: Scramblers are rare enough that most have been half-restored at least once, so trust nothing. Change every fluid, grease every fitting, check the ignition and carburetor, and look at the AMC 20 hubs. Capacities below are from ExtremeTerrain's CJ chart, which covers the 1981–86 drivetrains.

items.note: Look for rear-main and valve-cover leaks while you're under there.

items.note: Fit a fresh one before you judge the carburetor.

items.note: The 258 fires 1-5-3-6-2-4. Duraspark pickups and modules are common culprits for poor running.

items.spec: 50/50 coolant · 4.2 L: 10.5 qt · Iron Duke: 7.8 qt · AMC 2.5: 11 qt
items.note: Flush until clean, fit a new thermostat and check the overflow bottle for cracks.
